200.description: Query result, with per-field errors when a field could not be resolved

400.description: Malformed query, or a depth/complexity/alias limit was exceeded

TimeControl.description: Chess time control. All durations are in milliseconds.

refreshToken.description: Opaque, single-use refresh token. Also set as an httpOnly cookie for browser clients; non-browser API clients read it from the response body.

RefreshRequest.description: Refresh token request. The refresh token may be provided in the JSON body (non-browser API clients) or via the httpOnly `gambit_refresh` cookie (browser flow). The cookie is preferred when both are present.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token. Optional — may be provided via the httpOnly cookie instead.

color.description: Human player's color preference. Defaults to 'random'.

SearchDisplay.description: What a client needs to render the hit without fetching the entity again. Built only from data the entity’s own public view already exposes.

variables.description: Values for the variables the query declares

id.description: A specific catalogue entry. Mutually exclusive with the filters: a request carrying both is refused, because the two express different intentions and silently honouring one would hide the caller mistake that produced them.

CoachRequest.description: A position to coach, and optionally a move played in it and the sequence that reached it. There is deliberately no depth, nodes, movetime, multiPv, threshold, provider, model, temperature or token field: every one of those is server-owned policy, and a request that could name them would be choosing how much of a shared engine to spend on itself. What the caller controls is which questions apply — omitting "move" means there is no move to judge — never how expensively they are answered.

SubmitStudyPartnerTurnRequest.description: The intended move and the session version observed by the client. Current and next FEN, coaching policy, provider settings, and progress are server-owned and cannot be supplied.

StudyPartnerExplanation.description: Grounded explanation with citation, without provider or model metadata.

CommentaryCitation.description: What the engine said about the position the final move was played from. Separate from the prose beside it so a reader can tell a measurement from a sentence.

TournamentGameCommentaryResponse.description: Commentary on a finished tournament game. Every field but "commentary" is server-derived from the tournament aggregate and the durable game log; the request carries path identifiers and an empty body, so no value here can be an assertion the caller made. "fen" is the position the final move was played from, not the position it produced — the engine is never pointed at a board a game has already been decided on, and never at a game still being played.

white.description: Display handle, never an account id.

black.description: Display handle, never an account id.

tournamentResult.description: What the tournament recorded for this pairing, or null while it has not recorded one. A different fact from "result": the log says how the game ended, the aggregate says how the tournament scored it, and a director can make them disagree.

commentary.description: Model prose. Never the source of any fact above it.

RoundRecapPairing.description: One pairing as the tournament recorded it. "result" uses the vocabulary of the aggregate, which is wider than a game result: a bye and a void are how a round resolves a pairing nobody played.

black.description: Null for a bye, which has no opponent.

player.description: Display handle, never an account id.

TournamentRoundRecapResponse.description: A narrative recap of a round every pairing of which has a result. "results" and "standings" are computed from the tournament aggregate — the standings as they stood at the end of this round, not as they stand now — and the model is given them rather than asked for them. A round still in progress is refused rather than described.

pairingsNarrated.description: How many of "results" the narrative was given. Byes, voids and double forfeits have no spelling in the match vocabulary of the narrator, so they are published here and withheld from the prompt; when this is below results.length, the prose covers fewer games than the round contained.

narrative.description: Model prose. Never the source of any fact above it.
